title: The Fourfold Pattern
coreMove: classify a gamble by gain or loss and high or low probability before predicting risk appetite
sourcePressure: shows that risk preferences flip depending on whether outcomes are framed as gains or losses and as likely or unlikely
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: saying people are simply risk-averse or risk-seeking

hook: opening with a named bias definition for The Fourfold Pattern
starting in a lecture hall or generic seminar
counterintuition: the obvious advice is simply slow down
smart people are immune if they know the term
tryThisNow: write three lessons in a journal
examples: student in a classroom guessing an answer
